cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: One Thing Leads to Another
cards.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved replacing the sink. That dripping tap has exposed an opportunity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we just fit this washer? I've already bought it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Washer use is approved once the sink is out. Then we can replace the swollen worktop properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Removal of the cupboards is authorized. You may start emptying them; with the kitchen bare, we can finally correct the whole layout.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 permits the small washer only after sink removal and A5 authorizes cupboard removal to pursue a larger layout correction.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 bought washer causes A3 incorporation into a bigger repair; B4 worktop extent causes A5 clearing the whole kitchen.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers an economical fix and B4 warns of a real dependency, giving A independent practical contributions to expand.

heightening.evidence: B4 scope warning becomes A5 authorization for the broadest disruption yet.

specificity.evidence: A1 drip, B2 washer, A3 swollen worktop and B4 all cupboards establish concrete escalating work.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 finally-correct-the-layout phrase is earned by the cleared-kitchen opportunity created from B4 warning.
